public_spec:
Title: Refund function with no double refund

Behavior requirements:
- refund(amount) must accept a positive amount.
- refund(amount) must not exceed the remaining refundable balance.
- refunds on cancelled orders must fail.
- successful refunds must update refunded_total so the same funds cannot be refunded twice.

Edge cases:
- amount <= 0 should fail with appropriate error.
- amount > remaining refundable balance should fail.
- order status cancelled should cause refund to fail even if amount <= balance.
- refunding identical amount twice should fail on second attempt due to updated refunded_total.
- floating point precision or currency rounding should be handled consistently (e.g., use integer cents).
- initial refunded_total is 0 and remaining refundable balance equals total refundable amount.

Acceptance criteria:
- refund(positive_amount) succeeds when amount <= remaining refundable balance and order not cancelled.
- refund(positive_amount) on cancelled orders fails.
- refunded_total increases by amount on successful refund.
- subsequent refund attempts of the same funds are rejected due to updated refunded_total.
- refund amount must be strictly positive; zero or negative fails.

Non-goals:
- handling non-monetary refunds (e.g., store credits) unless specified.
- synchronization across distributed systems beyond the function boundary.
- audit logging details beyond correctness of state changes.

Testable assertions:
- assert refund(10) returns success and refunded_total == 10 when remaining balance >= 10 and order != cancelled.
- assert refund( fraud ) fails; improper type rejected.
- assert refund(0) fails.
- assert refund(remaining_balance) succeeds and refunded_total equals total refundable amount.
- assert after refund, refund(1) fails if remaining balance is 0 (no double refund).
- assert refund on cancelled order fails regardless of amount.
